article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 70% Indica / 30% Sativa
Genetics: Skunk × Northern Light × El Niño
Breeder: Green House Seed Company
THC Content: 19.8%
CBD Content: 0.12%
Terpene Profile: Myrcene , alpha-pinene
Primary Flavors: Sweet Skunk, apple, earth, spice
Flowering Time (Indoor): 9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: End of September
Indoor Yield: Up to 800 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: Up to 1,000 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy to intermediate

Big Bang comes from an era when a cannabis strain was expected to prove itself in the garden as convincingly as it did in the smoking room. Green House Seed Company developed the cultivar by combining Skunk, Northern Light, and El Niño, three genetic influences associated with very different strengths: pungent aroma and vigor from Skunk, compact resinous growth and physical relaxation from Northern Light, and a more complex tropical-Haze dimension through El Niño. The result is a short, broad marijuana plant capable of producing unusually heavy crops while retaining enough aromatic and psychoactive complexity to avoid becoming merely a production strain. Green House lists the finished cultivar at 70% indica and 30% sativa, with 19.8% THC and a terpene profile led by myrcene, alpha-pinene, and caryophyllene.

Its reputation was strengthened by competition recognition during the height of Amsterdam cannabis culture . Green House Seed Company’s official award history lists Big Bang as taking 3rd place at the 2000 High Times Cannabis Cup , placing it alongside the breeder’s better-known Cup-winning and Cup-placing genetics from the period. That distinction matters because the cultivar was competing during an era dominated by influential Dutch seed houses, established coffeeshops, and some of the strains that would shape cannabis breeding for decades afterward.

The name fits its horticultural personality as much as its effect. Big Bang can develop broad lateral growth and large, dense, trichome-covered flowers, creating considerably more canopy than its relatively short height might suggest. The experience is substantial but generally less aggressive than many modern ultra-high-THC cultivars. A calming physical effect develops around a pleasant mental ease, while the flavor moves between sweet Skunk, apple-like fruit, spice, earth, and floral pungency. For growers interested in classic European breeding and consumers who prefer balanced weed over sheer cannabinoid intensity, it remains one of the more practical older Green House hybrids.
Genetics and Lineage

The direct pedigree is Skunk × Northern Light × El Niño. Green House Seed Company describes these three parents as legendary strains and says the final selection was made with production, aromatic quality, and a balanced effect in mind. The family tree combines several of the most important genetic directions in late twentieth-century cannabis breeding. Skunk contributes vigorous hybrid performance and unmistakable pungency, Northern Light reinforces compact structure and dense resinous flowers, while El Niño brings a broader Haze , Skunk, Brazilian, and South Indian genetic background into the cross.

Northern Light has a particularly visible influence on plant architecture. Big Bang grows wider than it does tall, producing numerous lateral branches rather than relying entirely on one vertical stem. That squat growth pattern is useful indoors because cultivators can spread the canopy horizontally and maintain relatively even light exposure. Skunk adds additional branch vigor and the strong aromatic foundation, while El Niño contributes complexity to both the effect and fragrance.

Genetically, the cross is also a snapshot of older breeding priorities. Rather than stacking several closely related dessert hybrids, Green House combined lines with distinctly different histories and selected plants that balanced those traits. The finished cultivar therefore expresses more variation than a simple candy-on-candy cross: sweetness can sit beside spice, earth can appear beneath floral fruit, and the initial mental effect can remain engaging even as the indica-heavy body relaxation develops.
Effects and Experience

Big Bang generally begins in a quieter fashion than its name might imply. The first stage can bring a noticeable easing of mental tension, a warmer mood, and a comfortable shift in sensory perception without the intense rush associated with highly stimulating sativa marijuana. Conversation can remain easy, music may become more immersive, and ordinary evening activities can feel more satisfying. Green House characterizes the effect as relaxing, calming, and balanced rather than overwhelmingly energetic.

Physical relaxation becomes increasingly noticeable as the experience continues. The body can feel heavier and more settled, particularly when larger amounts are consumed, while the mental side usually remains softer rather than completely foggy. This progression makes the strain better suited to late afternoon or evening for many consumers. Lower doses may still allow casual activity, whereas heavier consumption is more likely to encourage sitting down, eating, watching a movie, or preparing for bed.

At roughly 19.8% THC according to the breeder, the cultivar falls below the laboratory numbers attached to many contemporary strains, but that should not be interpreted as weak weed. Potency is shaped by dose, tolerance, cannabinoid balance, inhalation method, and individual physiology. Too much can still produce dizziness, dry mouth, slowed reaction time, impaired memory, anxiety, or substantial lethargy. Its comparatively smooth effect profile may actually make overconsumption easier for people who assume a relaxed high means minimal impairment.
Medical Benefits

Big Bang has long been presented by Green House Seed Company as a medicinally oriented strain , particularly in relation to pain, appetite, and relaxation. Those breeder claims are historically important to the cultivar’s reputation, but they should be separated from modern clinical evidence. There are no controlled trials showing that Big Bang itself treats pain, insomnia, appetite loss, or any other specific medical condition.

Cannabis and cannabinoid research more broadly provides some context. The National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health notes evidence suggesting modest benefit from cannabis or cannabinoids for some forms of chronic pain. Certain cannabinoid medicines also have established medical applications, while research involving sleep has produced some positive findings in people with underlying conditions. None of those results demonstrates that this individual marijuana cultivar will provide the same effect for a particular person.

Potential drawbacks deserve equal attention. THC can produce dizziness, drowsiness, anxiety, impaired concentration, and altered judgment, and cannabinoids may interact with some prescription medications. Medical cannabis patients should therefore rely on actual product testing, dose awareness, and appropriate professional guidance rather than treating a breeder’s historical description as a medical guarantee.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Big Bang offers an aromatic profile that feels distinctly old school beside the candy-heavy weed dominating many current dispensaries. Green House describes sweet and strong Skunk as one of the central influences, joined by earthy and spicy Northern Light characteristics and pungent notes inherited through El Niño. Some expressions also reveal floral sweetness and an apple-like quality, producing more fruit character than the genetic names might initially suggest.

The documented terpene profile helps explain that combination. Green House identifies myrcene, alpha-pinene, and caryophyllene among the most expressed terpenes. Myrcene can reinforce earthy, herbal, and musky qualities; alpha-pinene fits the fresher pine-like edge that sometimes appears around the sweetness; and caryophyllene is consistent with pepper and spice beneath the Skunk aroma. Terpene concentration still changes between individual crops, but the breeder-established dominant compounds provide a stronger foundation than generic assumptions based on the strain name.

On the palate, sweetness often appears first, with floral fruit and apple-like notes sitting over a classic pungent cannabis base. Earth and spice become more apparent through the middle of the smoke, while Skunk remains through the finish. Proper curing is important because lighter fruit and floral components disappear more rapidly than heavier earthy aromatics when flower is dried excessively or stored in warm conditions.
Growing Information

Big Bang was clearly bred with production in mind. Green House describes a very short, branchy, bushy plant that grows naturally wider than taller. Outdoors, typical plants may reach approximately 160–180 centimeters under normal conditions, but much of the usable canopy develops horizontally. That makes the strain particularly compatible with Screen of Green cultivation , a method specifically recommended by the breeder.

Indoor flowering takes approximately nine weeks when growers want full maturation and the complete cannabinoid profile. Green House notes that commercial growers can harvest around eight weeks, although allowing the additional week provides fuller maturity. Maximum breeder-listed indoor production reaches approximately 800 grams per square meter. Those figures represent optimized circumstances rather than guaranteed household yields; lighting, plant count, root volume, nutrition, climate control, training, and phenotype all influence final production.

Outdoors, the breeder places harvest around the end of September in the Northern Hemisphere, an appealing trait for growers who want to finish before deeper autumn weather becomes problematic. Production can reach approximately 1,000 grams per plant under favorable circumstances. Dense flowers and a branch-heavy structure mean airflow remains important during the final weeks, particularly when the canopy becomes crowded. Strategic pruning and training can improve light penetration and reduce humid pockets around developing buds.

The plant’s lateral growth makes canopy planning more useful than attempting to force vertical height. Growers using a screen can spread branches outward early, filling horizontal space before allowing numerous flower sites to rise through the canopy. Large buds may require support as weight accumulates. Because the flowers become dense and trichome covered, maintaining stable humidity and regular air movement late in bloom is especially important.

Harvest quality depends just as much on drying as cultivation. A rushed dry can flatten the floral, apple, and fresh herbal side of the aroma, leaving primarily earth and Skunk. Gradual moisture reduction followed by controlled curing better preserves the balance between sweetness, spice, pungency, and fruit that Green House selected into the finished cultivar.
FAQ
What strain is Big Bang?

Big Bang is a 70% indica / 30% sativa hybrid bred by Green House Seed Company from Skunk × Northern Light × El Niño. It combines compact, high-yielding plant structure with sweet Skunk, earth, spice, fruit, and relaxing effects.
Who bred the Big Bang strain?

Green House Seed Company created the classic photoperiod Big Bang covered here. The breeder also offers a separate Big Bang Auto, so the original photoperiod cultivar should not be confused with the later autoflowering version.
Did Big Bang win a High Times Cannabis Cup award?

Yes. Green House Seed Company’s official competition record lists Big Bang as taking 3rd place at the 2000 High Times Cannabis Cup. The result places the strain among Green House’s extensive collection of award-recognized cannabis genetics from the classic Amsterdam Cup era.
How strong is Big Bang?

Green House lists the cultivar at approximately 19.8% THC and 0.12% CBD. Actual cannabinoid levels can vary with phenotype, cultivation conditions, harvest maturity, storage, and laboratory methodology.
How long does Big Bang take to flower?

Green House recommends approximately nine weeks indoors for full maturity, although commercial flower can be harvested around eight weeks. Outdoors in the Northern Hemisphere, the breeder places harvest around the end of September.
Final Thoughts on Big Bang

Big Bang represents a different philosophy from many modern cannabis hybrids. Its success does not depend on extreme THC figures or a fashionable dessert pedigree. Green House Seed Company combined Skunk, Northern Light, and El Niño and selected for a practical mixture of yield, compact structure, aroma, resin, and balanced effects. The resulting plant grows wide rather than excessively tall, performs especially well under a screen, finishes outdoors relatively early, and can produce exceptionally heavy crops in optimized environments.

Its competitive history reinforces that reputation. Green House’s own Cannabis Cup records credit Big Bang with 3rd place at the 2000 High Times Cannabis Cup, putting the cultivar among the company’s award-recognized strains during one of the most influential periods in Amsterdam cannabis breeding. That placement provides historical context for a cultivar that might otherwise be overlooked beside Green House legends such as Super Silver Haze, El Niño, and Great White Shark .

Flavor is equally traditional. Sweet Skunk and floral fruit sit alongside earth, spice, herbs, and an occasional apple-like note, with myrcene, alpha-pinene, and caryophyllene giving the aromatic profile a clear chemical foundation. This makes Big Bang considerably different from contemporary strains built almost entirely around candy, tropical fruit, or creamy gas.

Its effects complete the picture. Approximately 19.8% THC produces plenty of potency without making raw cannabinoid concentration the cultivar’s defining feature. Relaxation gradually gains control while the mind remains comfortably engaged, creating a smoother experience than the explosive name might imply. For growers, the appeal lies in heavy production, compact architecture, and a manageable nine-week bloom. For cannabis enthusiasts, the deeper attraction is historical: Big Bang is an award-recognized Green House hybrid demonstrating how intelligently combined Skunk, Northern Light, and El Niño genetics can deliver yield, flavor, resin, and enjoyable effects without relying on modern hype.
